name: Ubi
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

new_statements.quote: Dans l'état actuel de nos connaissances sur la langue, nous ne pouvons qu'émettre l'hypothèse de l'existence de trois tons en ubi, notamment haut ('), moyen non marqué graphiquement ici et bas (`). Exemples: díidé …
new_statements.translation: In the present state of our knowledge of the language, we can only put forward the hypothesis that there are three tones in Ubi, namely high ('), mid (not marked graphically here) and low (`). Examples: díidé …
new_statements.citation: Alio, Khalil. 2004. Préliminaires à une étude de la langue kajakse d'Am-Dam, de toram du Salamat, d'ubi du Guéra et de masmaje du Batha-Est (Tchad). In Gábor Takács (ed.), Egyptian and Semito-Hamitic (Afro-Asiatic) Studies in Memoriam Werner Vycichl, 229–285. Leiden: Brill.
new_statements.locator: Ubi section, remarks on tons (chapter pp. 229–285); exact page not verifiable from Google Books snippet view — a parallel tone passage in the same chapter carries the running header 'KAJAKSE, TORAM, UBI ET MASMAJE 279'
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ubi is treated as a three-level tone language (H, M, L), tentatively; the visible text makes no statement about word stress or a stress-like accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none visible; the author flags the three-tone analysis itself as a hypothesis
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on citation-form words (examples díidé 'bird', deenya 'saliva', cùwà 'tree' per the snippet summary). Quote assembled from overlapping Google Books snippets of a paywalled Brill chapter, not from an opened page; confidence accordingly medium.
new_statements.identity_note: Alio 2004 describes Ubi of the Guéra (Tunkul/Mongo area, canton Bidiyo), the same variety as ubii1238; no dialect split is reported (the SIL survey found no pronunciation differences across the six Ubi villages).
